title: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha (a Palestinian Amora of the Third Generation)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha. (A Palestinian Amora of the third generation.) He merited to receive from Rabbi Yochanan, as stated explicitly in Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:3, where he said: “I saw a thing: Resh Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan, and I do not know what he said to him.” Rabbi Zeira said to him: “Perhaps,” etc. Likewise we find that he spoke in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:2, Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:6, Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 4:1,

Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 1:1, Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 1:6 and Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:2. Hyman likewise places his traditions among the sages of the generation before Rabbi Yochanan, as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:1, additional locator ב־ג, where he spoke in Chizkiyah’s name; and in Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan, chapter 1, end of halakhah 2, and Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 5:1: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in the name of Rabbi Chananyah of Berat Chavrin (דברת חוורין).”

In Berakhot 23a and 49a: “Rabbi Ila said that Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said in the name of our master,” and Rashi explains there, 23a, that he is Rav. In the name of Rabbi Yoshiyah: Sukkah, beginning of chapter 1. In the name of Rabbi Yannai: Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 4:4; and in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:1, additional locator ב: — “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said that the school of Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak — one derives,” etc. In the name of Shmuel: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 6, end of halakhah 1.

In the name of Rabbi Yonatan: Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 3:1, Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4. In the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Moed Katan 22a (but there Hyman proposes the reading Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha bar Idi, as at the end of Demai, chapter 1). In the name of Rabbi Simlai: Moed Katan 16b. In the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 4:3, Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:4; and in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 4:3: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said: Akavya asked Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.”

Hyman says that he likewise received from all the great students of Rabbi Yochanan and the sages of his generation, as we find that he spoke in Rabbi Elazar’s name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 2:2 (Seder HaDorot reads Rabbi Yaakov bar Chama). In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:1: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Alexa in the name of Chizkiyah.” From Rabbi Assi he received much, as we find “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said that Rabbi Assi said,” as in Taanit 26b,

Moed Katan 26b (Hyman proposes this reading in Nedarim 56b, where the word Assi is missing), Zevachim 115b (Hyman proposes this reading there, 55b, instead of the supplied Rav Ashi — Dikdukei Soferim), Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:4, Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5, additional locator יב:, Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 2:5, and Yevamot, beginning of halakhah 2 of chapter 1. He was so important to Rabbi Assi that he called him (not in his presence) “our colleague,” as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:5: “Rabbi Yasa asked the physician of Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha:

What is the condition of the tooth of Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, our colleague?” In the name of Rabbi Ba bar Mamal: Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:1, additional locator ט:; and in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin, chapter 8, end of halakhah 3: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Ba bar Hamnuna in the name of Rav Ada bar Achavah.” In the name of Rav Hamnuna: Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 1, end of halakhah 5. In the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Ba: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:5,

Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1; and in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 16:2: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Chinena of Carthage in the name of Rabbi Hoshayah.” In the name of Rabbi Tavlai: Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:2. In the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi: Rosh Hashanah, beginning of chapter 3. In the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:7, Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 1:2. In the name of Rabbi Yitzchak bar Natan: Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 2:3,

Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:2. In the name of Rabbi Ulla of Caesarea in the name of Rabbi Chanina: Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, chapter 3, end of halakhah 2. In the name of Rav Shmuel bar Abba: Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6:5. In the name of Rav Shaman bar Abba: Moed Katan 16b; Niddah, beginning of chapter 3. His colleagues we find:

Rabbi Avuna, as in Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:5 and Yoma 1:1, additional locator ד:; and we find that he spoke in Rabbi Avuna’s name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 7:3 and Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 8:6. Rabbi Avdumi the Sailor, as at the end of Bava Metzia, chapter 4. Rabbi Abbahu, as in Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:4, additional locator יב:, where they said: “Yosha, the brother of Durai, had a case; he came and asked Rabbi Abbahu, who said to him … Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said to him: I was with you when you asked

Rabbi Avduma of Haifa … He said to him: I did not hear [it]; if you heard [it], go out and rule.” Rabbi Imi, for both spoke in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:4. Likewise Rabbi Zeira — although we find “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said that Rabbi Zeira said,” as in Berakhot 23a and Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:4, additional locator יב:, he was his colleague, as in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot, chapter 8, end of halakhah 3, where he said to Rabbi Zeira, “I was with you”; and as in Yoma 1:1,

additional locator ד: — Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Chanina (colleague of the Rabbis) were eating; Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha took the cup and blessed, and did not say “Let us bless.” Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to him, “And why did you not say …?” He said to him … “and the punctilious criticize him for that.” Rabbi Zeira was upset with him (Hyman explains that Rabbi Zeira was angry with him) for calling Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba punctilious. As in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:8: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha and Rabbi Zeira both said — one in the name of Mar Ukvan

and one in the name of Rav Nachman bar Yehudah. In Hyman’s reconstruction, Rabbi Chananyah, colleague of the Rabbis, was also older than he, as in Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 11:5, where he said, “Rabbi Chananyah, colleague of the Rabbis, disagreed,” etc.; and Hyman considers it plain that Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba was like his teacher, as we brought above that he spoke in his name. In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:3: Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Yitzchak had a case and sent Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba

(meaning that he sent him to ask Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba; Hyman considers this plain and clear, and argues that Mavo HaYerushalmi, entry Rabbi Yaakov bar Abba, erred in this, thinking that Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak asked Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha). Those who speak in his name: We find Rabbi Ami (the Babylonian), as in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:2. Rabbi Chaggai, as at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Orlah, chapter 3, who said: “When I came down from a ship, I heard the voice of Rabbi Yaakov

bar Acha.” Rabbi Chizkiyah was like his student-colleague, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:6, additional locator כא.: Rabbi Ami (the Babylonian), Rabbi Chizkiyah, Rabbi Kohen and Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha were strolling in the streets of Tzippori … Rabbi Chizkiyah said to Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, “Do not say anything to him”; and there, 2:5: “Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha were sitting in one place,” etc. And Rabbi

Chizkiyah spoke in his name there, 2:2; and in Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 3:4 it reads Rabbi Chizkiyah bar Yaakov bar Acha, and Hyman proposes “in the name of Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha.” Rabbi Yehudah Nesia (III), as in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:5, who asked him. Rabbi Yose said: “I posed a difficulty before Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha,” as in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 6:4; and in Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:4 Rabbi Yose said to him: “Do you remember that you were

saying, you and Rabbi Yirmeyah, in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish?”; and likewise in Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, he spoke in his name. Rabbi Yirmeyah in his name: Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 4:3. Rabbi Mana said to Rabbi Chizkiyah: “Do you remember that Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha stood here?” as in Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 7:1. The Rabbis of Caesarea in his name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4. Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyya of Kefar Akko

in his name, as in Moed Katan 16b. He is likewise mentioned in Sanhedrin 56a, where he found in the aggadah book of the school of Rav: “A descendant of Noah can be sentenced to death by a single judge,” etc. Of his personal matters we find in Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 2:5 that Kahana was appointed before Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, and nevertheless he [Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha] went in before Kahana for the intercalation. He [Kahana] said: “So the master of the teaching does not uphold it”

(for Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha had said there in Rabbi Yasa’s name that for intercalation one follows [the order of] appointment). Hyman suggests that his residence was Chamat Gader, as in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:2 and the end of the tractate there, where Rabbi Ami (the Babylonian) and Rabbi Yehudah Nesia (III), when they came there, asked him. We find in Moed Katan 25b (according to the reading of Dikdukei Soferim and Ein Yaakov): when Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha died, stars were seen
in the sky by day.
